set.st: In September 1962 a power-shovel operator digging a ditch on the Marg fur farm broke open a pint fruit jar inside a pail about 18 inches down. It held $56.30 in silver dimes through dollars, all dated in the 1800s. LiDAR cache check (USGS 1 m, 2018): Nothing that fits the story stands out within the search area: the pits and lines it finds there are ditches, banks, ponds or natural ground. The farm was the Marg Fur Food Ranch (owner Kurt Marg, there 50 years), so the jar was older than his time on it; earlier owners who hid one jar may have hidden others. Find the Marg farm on a 1960s Clark County plat. The farm was the Kurt Marg mink farm, probably his parents Frank Marg Sr.'s land. The jar sat 2 ft deep inside a galvanized pail and held only 1800s coins. No second jar was reported. Where: the Marshfield News-Herald (27 Sep 1962, p. 8) says 2.5 mi NW of Neillsville, the Clark County Press 3 mi W; they disagree by about 3 km, so the pin stays put.
set.tovw: Lead grade F: found and counted 1962, two period prints; nothing left open
